result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens in sync mode returns a raw fetch Response (from fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT...)), while the Hubspot call site binds this to HubspotToken and (per the surrounding context visible in the diff, 'set expiry date as offset from current time') reads token fields from it. A fetch Response has no own enumerable token properties, so the resulting persisted credential key would be corrupted on the first sync-mode refresh. The mechanism is grounded in the diff's explicit return of the fetch Response and its consumption as a typed token object.

judged_text: In sync mode the fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens is bound to HubspotToken, so expiresIn/accessToken reads yield undefined and the persisted key collapses to {expiryDate: NaN} because a fetch Response has no own enumerable properties to spread. The first Hubspot token refresh under credential sharing wipes the stored credential key, destroying the access and refresh tokens and breaking the integration until the user re-authenticates.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`) without calling `.json()`. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. Under sync mode this value will be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so any subsequent reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` / `expiresIn` (or spreading it into persisted credentials) will yield `undefined`/bad data and can corrupt the stored credential update. The diff shows this type/shape mismatch is introduced by the change.
